mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening periods (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 8% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to expectations of slower wage growth and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not statistically different from negative returns when UNRATE > 8% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private demand) exceeds 13,500 in the prior quarter, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive, reflecting stronger consumer and business demand boosting earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 > 13500 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO above 95.0 signals supply-side weakness, leading to a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO < 95.0 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST (industrial production) above their prior month levels jointly predict a positive S&P 20-day forward return, reflecting accommodative policy and strong demand.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS up from prior month AND HOUST up from prior month
regime_hint: coordinated monetary accommodation and production expansion
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when both proxies rise (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS below 130,000 in the prior month signals labor market weakness, associated with a negative S&P 60-day forward return due to reduced consumer confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS falls (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly RSAFS (retail sales) exceeds 400,000 for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is positive, indicating resilient consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during the two-month RSAFS expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime where CPIAUCSL exceeds 220 for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to persistent inflation eroding real earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative during the three-month inflation spike (p > 0.05).
